forecast-period.text: A trough of low pressure lingers about the east, before weakening from late Wednesday. A slow moving high pressure system in the Tasman Sea will re-establish a ridge across southern parts from Wednesday. A trough is then forecast to briefly move into the west on Thursday, before another trough and cold front move more broadly across SA on Friday and Saturday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the northwest, also possible about central and eastern districts, clearing by the evening. Maximum temperatures above average. Southeast to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Showers and thunderstorms in the east and northwest. Thunderstorms possibly severe with heavy rainfall which may lead to flash flooding, with a slight risk of damaging wind gusts and large hail as well, mainly about the Mid North and southeast. Southwest to southeasterly winds.

Areas of morning fog in the south. Showers and possible thunderstorms across the north. Thunderstorms may be severe in the far northwest with damaging wind gusts and large hail possible. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average near the coasts. East to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes. Winds tending north to northwesterly ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change in the west during the day.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the north, developing about central and eastern districts from the afternoon. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average in the south. East to northeasterly winds, tending southeast to southwesterly winds in the far west. Winds then shifting northeast to northwesterly ahead of a southwest to southerly change moving across during the day.

text.p: Showers and thunderstorms possible across most districts. Maximum temperatures above to near average, grading to below average in the west. South to southwesterly winds, tending north to northwesterly in the far northeast before the change moves across by the evening.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: 2 to 10 mm broadly across SA. Falls increasing to 5 to 15 mm about the agricultural areas, Flinders Ranges and the far northwest, with isolated totals between 15 to 25 mm possible. Heavier falls up to 40 mm are possible with severe thunderstorms in the southeast.
